about: illustrace stylebench human-judgment validation, batch_4. preregistered spec: survey/specs/batch_4.json. ground truth comes from parametric svg stimuli: the gt side is the one with the provably higher parameter (or the spec-declared hypothesis). anchor question is a warm-up and is not scored. catch pairs are identical images: 'no difference' is the correct answer.

questions.prompt: which linework looks more like multiple overlapping pen passes?
questions.note: warm-up, extreme scatter step, not scored — but see anchor rule in adaptive_rules
endpoint pair sigma 1.5 vs 4.5; stimulus validity gate
adjacent step 1.5 vs 3.0; the JND probe for lateral jitter

questions.prompt: which linework thins more toward its ends?
questions.note: profile shape discrimination, ink-matched: constant vs symmetric taper

questions.prompt: which linework varies more in thickness along the stroke?
questions.note: profile shape discrimination, ink-matched: constant vs mid-stroke bulge — the profile case plain taper cannot express

questions.prompt: which linework fades out more toward one end?
questions.note: endpoint pair alpha 1.0 vs 0.10 falloff. prompt deliberately says 'toward one end' not 'along the stroke' — falloff renders along the bbox-dominant axis, so per-stroke direction varies; this tests depth, not axis

questions.prompt: which linework fades out more toward one end?
questions.note: adjacent step 0.45 vs 0.10; JND probe for falloff depth

questions.prompt: which linework looks more like multiple overlapping pen passes?
questions.note: adjacent step 0 vs 3 sigma scatter at passes=2; JND probe for pass misalignment

questions.prompt: which linework looks more like multiple overlapping pen passes?
questions.note: rotation-only misalignment 0 vs 4 deg at passes=2; tests that rotation separates from scatter as a distinct pass-misalignment cue
